ADR-0001 / LYZ-54 observations and limits:
- Observed: IPv6 then IPv4 heavy TCP A -> C through B, all four TAP RX and guest interface RX counters unchanged during a two-second settled hold; post-T ICMP probes fail; receiver pause/resume does not change guest RX; existing TCP resumes after thaw.
- Pre-T captured RX / Net::prepare_save: NOT OBSERVABLE. Aggregate guest RX deltas during settling cannot identify individual pre-T frames or deferred RX; no snapshot preparation is invoked.
- Post-T captured memory / virtio RX while paused: NOT OBSERVABLE directly. TAP counters and guest RX across resume are evidence of isolation, not inspection of virtio rings or guest-backed deferred RX buffers.
- TX completion versus serialization: NOT OBSERVABLE. No sender snapshot is created; counters cannot establish that a descriptor completion is serialized rather than pending for replay.
- Clone captured RX preservation / host-only queue omission: DEFERRED to LYZ-23 snapshot/restore. Fresh TAP queues are a design obligation, not a result of this test.
- Host paths: administrative TAP down rejects Firecracker userspace writes with EIO; retained per-file TAP RX queues may still deliver pre-T frames. In-flight writes and bridge completion at T cannot be classified individually by these counters. Post-T delivery after thaw is not classified by this test.
- Environment: CI uses Ubuntu's runner kernel, not the pinned developer host kernel; neither counters nor a passing run prove the pinned-kernel serialization boundaries.
